newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks closed mixed for holiday.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks closed mixed for holiday.

text.p: Argentine blue chips pulled back on profit-taking Wednesday but the broad market stayed in positive ground ahead of Thursday's May Day holiday.

"The market seesawed lower today because prices had notched up good gains and players turned cautious ahead of the break," said Jose Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli. "Economic indicators will keep coming out in the United States and nobody wants to be too exposed."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV shed 0.8 percent to 722.6, trimming gains so far in the week to 1.0 percent, while the broad market index added 0.3 percent.
The MerVal closed up 2.3 percent in April and faces short-term resistance at 735, dealers said.
"Now everything depend's on Friday's all-important U.S. jobs report -- we're bracing for a rocky ride but our guess is the data will be favorable," an analyst at a foreign investment bank said.
Floor volume remained strong at 30.2 million pesos against 29.2 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover picked up to 126.8 million pesos from 104.4 million Tuesday.
Losing issues outpaced winners 28 to 23 and 18 stocks closed flat.
"Trading has become very selective at the start of the company results period," Napoli said.
Worst main-tier performers were carmaker Ciadea, footmaker and textile firm Alpargatas and oil company Astra, which dropped 4.8 percent, 4.1 percent and 3.4 percent, respectively.
MerVal gains were led by Telefonica, holding company Perez Companc and steelmaker Siderca, which tacked on 2.2 percent, 1.6 percent and 0.7 percent, respectively.
